chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever drinks an intoxicant, his prayer will not be accepted from him for forty days. So if he dies during the forty days, he dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah); and if he repents, Allah turns towards him.

key_terms.تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: Allah turned towards him (accepted his repentance)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the prayer of someone who consumes intoxicants and dies before repenting?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi links the physical act of consuming intoxicants to a specific period of spiritual invalidity for prayer, emphasizing the severity of the sin by equating death in this state to the pre-Islamic 'Jahiliyyah.' It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interplay between ritual purity and divine mercy, noting that sincere repentance (tawbah) restores the individual's spiritual standing despite the temporary suspension of their prayers.
